title: How a tool call travels
lede: You pick a door and a tool in the browser. This lab's server sends the MCP call to the PingOne Privilege gateway with the door's agent key. The gateway checks who is calling and asks the policy. Only a permitted call reaches the MCP backend. The answer comes back as one of four outcomes, and the lab shows that word first.

refusal.label: Outcome: the call did not run

nodes.label: Browser
sub: You pick a door and a tool
The agent key is never here

nodes.label: Lab server
sub: Sends the MCP call, turns the answer into a verdict

nodes.label: Gateway door
sub: Checks the agent key and who it stands for

nodes.label: Policy check
sub: May this identity call this tool?

nodes.label: MCP backend
sub: Only a permitted call gets here

edges.label: 1. pick a door, run a tool
2. MCP call with the agent key
3. who is calling, and may they?

steps.title: Pick a door and a tool
steps.what: The page asks this lab's server to open one of the standing doors and call a tool. The agent key stays on the server.
steps.why: The browser never holds the key, so the page cannot leak it.

steps.title: Open the door with the agent key
steps.what: The lab starts the MCP session with the gateway, using the key for the door that was picked.
steps.why: The key decides which identity the gateway evaluates, not who is signed in to this page.

steps.title: Exchange the key for a token
steps.what: Inside the gateway the key is exchanged for a token. A client cannot see this step, so Mock shows it as illustrative and Real leaves it out.
steps.why: The policy decides about an identity, not about a key.

steps.title: Check the token
steps.what: The gateway introspects the token to learn who is calling. A client cannot see this step either.
steps.why: A bad or expired token is refused here, before any policy runs.

steps.title: Ask for the tools
steps.what: The lab asks the door which tools it offers. The gateway answers with only the tools this identity may see.
steps.why: Discovery is filtered by the same policy as a call.

steps.title: Ask for the tool to run
steps.what: The lab asks the door to run the tool that was picked, with the arguments typed in the page.
steps.why: A call is checked by the same policy as discovery, tool by tool.

steps.title: Ask the policy
steps.what: The gateway asks the policy whether this identity may call this tool. The answer is permit or refuse.
steps.why: This is the decision. Everything after it follows from it.

steps.title: The tool runs
steps.what: The call was permitted, so it reaches the MCP backend and the tool answers.
steps.why: Only a permitted call is ever dispatched.

steps.title: The backend did not answer
steps.what: The call was permitted and dispatched, but the backend failed to answer. This is an upstream error, not a policy decision.
steps.why: A refusal and a failure look alike on a screen. The path tells them apart.

steps.title: Refused before the backend
steps.what: The policy refused the call, so nothing reached the tool.
steps.why: A refusal is a correct answer, not an error.

steps.title: Held for a person
steps.what: The gateway holds the call until a person approves it. This lab simulates that hold.
steps.why: Some calls are allowed only with a human in the loop.

steps.title: The verdict is shown first
steps.what: The lab turns the gateway's answer into one word and shows it before the evidence.
steps.why: The outcome leads; the path explains it.
